resources.string: The code does not compile. Open the first error line: usually a missing import, a renamed symbol or a missing library.
A resource is missing or misnamed (layout, string, drawable). Make sure every @string and R.string is defined in values and values-en.
A dependency could not be fetched
The library or its version does not exist, the repository is not declared, or the network dropped. Check the version number and re-run.
The JDK in the workflow does not match what the project or Gradle needs. Change java-version in the setup-java step.
The SDK or its licences are not ready. Add a setup-android step or accept the licences.
The keystore or its passwords are missing or wrong. Check the secrets: KEYSTORE_BASE64, passwords and alias.
Version conflict or a missing package. Try clearing the cache, pin the right version, or add --legacy-peer-deps.
At least one test failed. Find the test name in the log and compare the expected result with the actual one.
A Python exception. The last line of the traceback is the cause; often a library missing from requirements or a typo.
The token lacks the permission. Add permissions: (for example contents: write) to the workflow or enable Read and write in the Actions settings.
A secret or input is missing
A required secret or input is not defined. Add it under Secrets or pass it in with: on the step.
A file or command is missing
The path is wrong or the command is not installed. Remember file names are case-sensitive on Linux and the working-directory may differ.
The process used all the runner memory. Raise org.gradle.jvmargs, lower parallelism or split the build.
The operation took longer than allowed or the network dropped. Re-run; if it repeats raise timeout-minutes or enable caching.
The YAML structure is wrong (indentation or a missing colon). The line named in the message is the first place to look.
The action name or version is wrong, or the input is not supported. Check owner/name@version and the with: names.
The runner ran out of space. Delete old caches and artifacts or clean up before building.
A temporary connection failure or a rate limit. Re-run only the failed jobs; it usually passes.
The formatting or lint tool rejected the code. Run the formatter locally or fix the lines it lists.
The image or a Dockerfile command failed. Check the image name and tag and that the RUN commands succeed.
The push or pull was refused: permission, a protected branch or newer history. Pull the latest changes or check branch protection.
A command in the step failed
A command ended with an error code and no more specific pattern matched. Open the first error line in the log.
No known pattern found. Open the first error line in the log and start there.
Local rule-based analysis, offline, and not always exact.
There is no failed job in this run.
Touches workflow files: it can change how builds behave.
Includes a sensitive file name (key or env). Make sure it leaks no secrets.
Large deletion: removed lines are more than twice the added ones.
Includes binary or large files with no text diff.
Touches AndroidManifest: permissions or components may change.
